gaps.concept: Preeclampsia thresholds: blood pressure ≥140/90 mm Hg and proteinuria ≥300 mg/day or protein:creatinine ratio ≥0.3; severe hypertension is ≥160/110.
gaps.why_tested: A vignette gives exact blood pressure and urine values and asks for the diagnosis or severity.

gaps.concept: Chronic hypertension with new proteinuria or organ dysfunction after 20 weeks indicates superimposed preeclampsia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with hypertension before pregnancy develops new findings in the third trimester.

gaps.concept: Major preeclampsia risk factors include prior preeclampsia, first pregnancy, multifetal gestation, chronic hypertension, kidney disease, diabetes, and molar pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which pregnant patient is most likely to develop preeclampsia.

gaps.concept: Preeclampsia causes glomerular endotheliosis: swollen glomerular endothelial cells narrow capillary lumens and produce proteinuria.
gaps.why_tested: A renal biopsy or mechanism question accompanies hypertension and proteinuria in pregnancy.

gaps.concept: HELLP hemolysis is microangiopathic, with schistocytes, elevated LDH, and indirect bilirubin.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient has right upper quadrant pain, thrombocytopenia, and fragmented red cells.

gaps.concept: Preeclampsia and eclampsia can first present after delivery.
gaps.why_tested: A recently postpartum patient develops severe headache, hypertension, visual symptoms, or seizures.

gaps.concept: Gestational diabetes risk factors include obesity, prior gestational diabetes or macrosomic infant, polycystic ovary syndrome, and family history of diabetes.
gaps.why_tested: A stem asks which patient warrants early diabetes screening or has the highest risk.

gaps.concept: High-risk patients may be tested for previously unrecognized diabetes at the first prenatal visit; routine gestational screening remains at 24–28 weeks.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with major diabetes risk factors presents early in pregnancy and the question asks when to test.

gaps.concept: Maternal glucose crosses the placenta, but maternal insulin does not; fetal hyperglycemia stimulates fetal pancreatic β-cell hyperplasia.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks why maternal diabetes causes fetal overgrowth and neonatal hypoglycemia.

gaps.concept: Fetal hyperinsulinemia delays surfactant production, increasing neonatal respiratory distress despite macrosomia.
gaps.why_tested: A large infant of a diabetic mother develops respiratory distress shortly after birth.

gaps.concept: Diabetic embryopathy follows hyperglycemia during organogenesis; diabetes first developing late in pregnancy does not cause those early structural defects.
gaps.why_tested: A question contrasts congenital malformations in pregestational diabetes with complications of gestational diabetes.

gaps.concept: Maternal diabetic vasculopathy can cause placental insufficiency and fetal growth restriction despite diabetes’ usual association with macrosomia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with longstanding diabetes and vascular disease has a growth-restricted fetus.

gaps.concept: Transvaginal ultrasound identifies placenta previa by placental coverage of the internal cervical os.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with painless third-trimester bleeding needs a test to locate the placenta.

gaps.concept: Accreta attaches to myometrium, increta invades myometrium, and percreta penetrates through serosa, sometimes reaching the bladder.
gaps.why_tested: A pathology or imaging stem asks for the depth of abnormal placental invasion.

gaps.concept: Placenta accreta spectrum may show placental lacunae and loss of the normal placental–myometrial interface on ultrasound.
gaps.why_tested: A patient with prior cesarean delivery and previa has a characteristic prenatal ultrasound.

gaps.concept: Placental abruption may cause concealed hemorrhage; external bleeding can underestimate blood loss and shock.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has severe abdominal pain and a rigid uterus with little visible bleeding.

gaps.concept: Vasa previa is associated with velamentous cord insertion or a succenturiate placental lobe; membrane rupture causes fetal bradycardia despite maternal stability.
gaps.why_tested: Bleeding immediately after membrane rupture is accompanied by sudden fetal distress.

gaps.concept: An indirect Coombs test detects maternal anti-RBC antibodies; a direct Coombs test detects antibodies bound to neonatal RBCs.
gaps.why_tested: A Rh-negative mother and an anemic, jaundiced newborn have different antibody tests.

gaps.concept: Anti-D immunoglobulin provides passive antibody before maternal sensitization and cannot reverse established anti-D alloimmunization.
gaps.why_tested: A question asks why prophylaxis helps an unsensitized mother but not one with a positive antibody screen.

gaps.concept: Increased fetal middle cerebral artery peak systolic velocity suggests anemia from maternal RBC alloimmunization.
gaps.why_tested: A sensitized mother’s fetus undergoes Doppler evaluation for hemolytic anemia.

gaps.concept: ABO hemolytic disease can affect a first pregnancy, often involves a type O mother, and is usually milder than Rh disease.
gaps.why_tested: A firstborn infant develops jaundice despite no prior maternal sensitization.

gaps.concept: Preterm labor requires regular contractions with cervical change before 37 weeks; prior preterm birth and short cervix increase risk.
gaps.why_tested: A patient has contractions, and the stem asks whether they represent true preterm labor.

gaps.concept: A short cervix increases preterm birth risk; a negative fetal fibronectin test predicts low short-term delivery risk.
gaps.why_tested: A symptomatic patient has uncertain preterm labor and receives cervical length or fibronectin testing.

gaps.concept: Terbutaline’s β2-agonism can cause maternal tachycardia, hyperglycemia, and hypokalemia.
gaps.why_tested: A patient receiving tocolysis develops palpitations or abnormal glucose and potassium values.

gaps.concept: Rupture of membranes is supported by fluid pooling, alkaline nitrazine testing, and microscopic ferning on sterile speculum examination.
gaps.why_tested: A patient reports a gush of fluid before labor and the question asks how to confirm membrane rupture.

gaps.concept: Preterm prelabor rupture of membranes increases ascending infection risk; latency antibiotics can prolong pregnancy when infection is absent.
gaps.why_tested: A patient’s membranes rupture weeks before term without fever or labor.

gaps.concept: Chorioamnionitis presents with maternal fever plus findings such as fetal tachycardia, uterine tenderness, or purulent fluid; treat with antibiotics and delivery.
gaps.why_tested: A patient develops fever and fetal tachycardia after prolonged membrane rupture.

gaps.concept: Fetal growth restriction is estimated weight or abdominal circumference below the 10th percentile; asymmetric head sparing suggests placental insufficiency.
gaps.why_tested: Ultrasound shows a small abdomen with relatively preserved head size.

gaps.concept: Absent or reversed umbilical artery end-diastolic flow indicates severe placental resistance in fetal growth restriction.
gaps.why_tested: A growth-restricted fetus has abnormal Doppler waveforms and the question asks what they imply.

gaps.concept: Oligohydramnios follows reduced fetal urine production, placental insufficiency, or membrane rupture; severe early oligohydramnios causes pulmonary hypoplasia.
gaps.why_tested: Low fluid accompanies fetal renal abnormality or placental disease, and the stem asks for a consequence.

gaps.concept: Polyhydramnios can result from impaired fetal swallowing, including esophageal or duodenal atresia and anencephaly.
gaps.why_tested: Excess fluid accompanies a fetal anomaly despite normal maternal glucose.

gaps.concept: A reactive nonstress test has at least two fetal heart-rate accelerations within 20 minutes; nonreactivity prompts further assessment.
gaps.why_tested: A high-risk pregnancy has a fetal heart-rate tracing, and the question asks whether it is reassuring.

gaps.concept: A biophysical profile scores fetal breathing, movement, tone, amniotic fluid, and nonstress testing; low scores suggest fetal compromise.
gaps.why_tested: A stem provides ultrasound and heart-rate findings and asks how to interpret fetal well-being.

gaps.concept: After 20 weeks, fundal height in centimeters approximates gestational age in weeks; a substantial discrepancy prompts growth or fluid assessment.
gaps.why_tested: A prenatal visit reports a uterine measurement smaller or larger than expected.

gaps.concept: PUPPP usually starts in abdominal striae and spares the umbilicus; pemphigoid gestationis often involves the umbilicus and forms tense bullae.
gaps.why_tested: A third-trimester pruritic eruption must be distinguished by distribution and blistering.

gaps.concept: Pemphigoid gestationis involves anti-BP180 antibodies and linear C3 deposition along the dermal–epidermal junction.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnant patient has periumbilical bullae and a skin immunofluorescence result.

gaps.concept: Intrahepatic cholestasis causes intense pruritus without a primary rash; excoriations may be present, and bile acids are elevated.
gaps.why_tested: A third-trimester patient has itching but no primary skin lesions.

gaps.concept: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy causes microvesicular steatosis, hypoglycemia, coagulopathy, and hepatic dysfunction, distinguishing it from HELLP.
gaps.why_tested: A late-pregnancy patient has vomiting, jaundice, low glucose, and prolonged clotting times.

gaps.concept: Fetal long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency is associated with maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy.
gaps.why_tested: A maternal liver-failure vignette asks for the fetal metabolic defect.

gaps.concept: Postterm pregnancy increases oligohydramnios and meconium-related risk as placental function declines; antepartum testing or induction may be used.
gaps.why_tested: A pregnancy extends beyond term and the question asks why fetal surveillance is warranted.

gaps.concept: Uterine rupture is associated with a prior uterine scar and presents during labor with sudden fetal bradycardia and loss of fetal station.
gaps.why_tested: A patient attempting vaginal birth after cesarean develops acute pain and fetal distress.

gaps.concept: Amniotic fluid embolism causes abrupt hypoxemia, hypotension, and disseminated intravascular coagulation during labor or shortly postpartum.
gaps.why_tested: A laboring patient suddenly collapses with respiratory failure and bleeding.
